item.title: Chinese Warship Locks Fire Control Radar on Philippine Warship, Manila Says
item.description: A Chinese corvette directed its fire control radar at one of Manila’s newest warships during an incident earlier this month in the South China Sea, according to the Philippine Navy. The March 7 encounter saw the People’s Liberation Army Navy Type 056A-class corvette Guang’an (622) point its Type 347 fire control radar at Philippine Navy BRP Miguel Malvar (FFG-6) while the frigate was conducting a sovereignty patrol near Sabina Shoal. item.title: U.S. Forces Strike Suspected Narco Boat in the Eastern Pacific
item.description: U.S. forces with Joint Task Force Southern Spear struck a vessel Thursday in the Eastern Pacific, the 46th such strike since Sept. 1, 2025. The strike on a boat suspected of carrying narcotics left three survivors, U.S. Southern Command announced Friday on social media site X. SOUTHCOM notified the U.S. Coast Guard to activate search and rescue for the three people. The U.S. has not provided an update on the search and rescue operations. item.title: Boxer Amphibious Ready Group, 11th MEU Deploy from California
item.description: The three ships that make up the Boxer Amphibious Ready Group with their embarked Marines deployed from the West Coast this week, USNI News has learned. The ARG and Marines with the 11th Marine Expeditionary Unit completed certification exercises, a Navy official confirmed to USNI News. item.title: Taiwan Receives First U.S. MQ-9 SkyGuardian Drones
item.description: Taiwan received the first batch of an advanced drone order from the U.S. last week that is set to bolster Taipei’s over-the-horizon targeting capabilities. The Ministry of National Defense oversaw the transfer of two MQ-9B SkyGuardian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) Tuesday from General Atomics. The drones are the latest in the American defense contractor’s line-up of Reaper-derived variants. item.title: French Navy Intercepts Suspected Russian Tanker in Western Mediterranean
item.description: The French Navy intercepted and seized a sanctioned Russian tanker suspected of flying a false flag Friday in the Western Mediterranean. The French Navy boarded tanker MT Deyna, flying a Mozambican flag as it sailed from Murmansk, Russia, according to a news release from the Maritime Prefecture of the Mediterranean. item.title: Carrier USS Gerald R. Ford Arrives in Souda Bay for Repairs After Laundry Room Fire
item.description: USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) pulled into port at Souda Bay, Greece, the Navy announced Monday. Ford, the flagship of the Gerald R. Ford Carrier Strike Group, is in port for maintenance and repairs following a March 12 fire in the aft laundry room. A ship spotter saw Ford and three destroyers head into the Suez Canal on Saturday. item.title: Destroyer USS Mustin Arrives at New Homeport in Japan
item.description: Destroyer USS Mustin (DDG-89) arrived Monday at its new forward-deployed homeport in Yokosuka, Japan, joining forward-deployed Destroyer Squadron 15. Mustin joins U.S. 7th Fleet after nearly five years in San Diego. This marks the second time the destroyer has been forward deployed to Yokosuka, having previously been deployed there from 2006 to 2021, according to a Navy release published the same day. “Mustin Nation is proud to return to Japan,” Cmdr. item.title: USS Gettysburg Back in Norfolk After 5 Months in SOUTHCOM
item.description: USS Gettysburg (CG-64) returned to Naval Station Norfolk, Va., on Monday after five months in the U.S. Southern Command area of responsibility. The Ticonderoga-class guided-missile cruiser left Norfolk in October and began operating in the Caribbean around Oct. 31, 2025, according to the USNI News Fleet and Marine Tracker.
